@Megan Daniel looking at all 3 options for CFR, but especially for the light theme against light website (probably, a common case) or for any other theme when the website background color is similar to the theme/Firefox UI color - the chevron connecting the CFR message and the browser UI is not clear and, with the similar colors of the website, it may seem that the message came from the website (like those never-ending popups and ads on some websites). 

Would that be possible to make the border of the CFR thicker and brighter? I think, if it would be the same color as the text color on the CFR, the current thickness would be sufficient - this would highlight that the shield icon from Firefox is saying something, not the website below it. WDYT?
@Megan Daniel recommending to put the Close button as item 2 in the screen reader order (refer to the comment above for details)

@Megan Daniel I assume those messages would be functioning as modals aka they would block interaction with the rest of the view until dismissed? Then we could use the "modal" role and pattern (linking MagentA11y because they have engineering notes far better than I could provide for mobile :sweat_smile: ).

If it would be functioning as a banner in the examples and would still allow a user to interact with the rest of the page, we could follow the tidbit pattern (a group with CTAs), especially if we expect there won't be more than 2 action buttons.

LMK if you have questions - happy to discuss other options/ideas too!

[Editing to add: now reviewing the rest of the page, it seems that there probably is a separation. If so, CFR could be "modal" and follow the linked pattern or implementing the custom component with the accessible name for the group - refer to the Magenta page for engineering details and QA references. And the Banner could follow the tidbit pattern: also a group with an accessible label but not restricting the user's interaction with the rest of the page.]

@Megan Daniel if we follow the visual reading order (in LTR languages, as in the example), the close button would be the item 2, and the actions are items 3 and 4. It may be justifiable to consider the "X" close button a second column in the reading order, but it would be a stretch. 

I'd recommended following the visual reading order to avoid confusion for sighted users of screen readers (i.e. those with low vision or cognitive disabilities).
